title: Entrepreneurship
source_note: Grounded in second-year entrepreneurship theory: feasibility studies, business plan components, sources of business finance, legal forms of enterprise, franchising, and small business marketing and operations, as taught in NUC-aligned Nigerian entrepreneurship programmes. Builds on ENT101 without repeating its introductory-level content.

questions.question: A feasibility study, in the context of starting a new venture, is primarily conducted to:
options: Determine whether a proposed business idea is practical and likely to succeed
Replace the need for any business registration
Calculate the founder's personal income tax only
Design the company's logo and letterhead
questions.correct_answer: Determine whether a proposed business idea is practical and likely to succeed
questions.explanation: A feasibility study systematically evaluates the market, technical, financial, and operational viability of a proposed venture before resources are committed.

questions.question: Market feasibility, as one component of a feasibility study, focuses on assessing:
options: Whether sufficient customer demand exists for the proposed product or service
The founder's personal credit history alone
The color scheme of the proposed shopfront
The national inflation rate over the past decade
questions.correct_answer: Whether sufficient customer demand exists for the proposed product or service
questions.explanation: Market feasibility examines target customers, competition, and demand levels to determine if the market can support the proposed business.

questions.question: Technical feasibility in a feasibility study primarily examines:
options: Whether the business has the necessary technology, equipment, and processes to deliver the product
The personal marital status of the founder
The number of holidays observed nationally
The color of competitors' logos
questions.correct_answer: Whether the business has the necessary technology, equipment, and processes to deliver the product
questions.explanation: Technical feasibility assesses whether the required production processes, equipment, and technical expertise are available and adequate.

questions.question: Financial feasibility assesses primarily whether:
options: The proposed venture can generate sufficient returns to justify the required investment
The business logo is aesthetically pleasing
The founder has any siblings
The business location has heavy rainfall
questions.correct_answer: The proposed venture can generate sufficient returns to justify the required investment
questions.explanation: Financial feasibility projects costs, revenues, and profitability to determine whether the venture is likely to be financially viable.

questions.question: The 'market analysis' section of a comprehensive business plan should typically include:
options: Industry overview, target market description, and competitor analysis
Only the founder's academic transcripts
A list of unrelated government holidays
The personal phone numbers of all employees
questions.correct_answer: Industry overview, target market description, and competitor analysis
questions.explanation: A market analysis situates the business within its industry, defines the target customers, and evaluates competitors to justify the business opportunity.

questions.question: The 'organizational and management plan' section of a business plan primarily describes:
options: The business's ownership structure, management team, and staffing
The projected cash flow for the next five years
The chemical composition of the product
The exchange rate between two foreign currencies
questions.correct_answer: The business's ownership structure, management team, and staffing
questions.explanation: This section outlines who runs the business, the organizational structure, and key personnel responsible for major functions.

questions.question: A break-even analysis in a business plan is used to determine:
options: The sales volume at which total revenue equals total costs
The maximum possible profit a business can ever earn
The exact date a business will close permanently
The founder's personal savings account balance
questions.correct_answer: The sales volume at which total revenue equals total costs
questions.explanation: Break-even analysis identifies the point where a business neither makes a profit nor a loss, helping entrepreneurs set realistic sales targets.

questions.question: Equity financing, as a source of business capital, involves:
options: Raising funds by selling ownership shares in the business
Borrowing money that must be repaid with interest
Receiving a non-repayable government grant only
Using only the founder's personal credit card
questions.correct_answer: Raising funds by selling ownership shares in the business
questions.explanation: Equity financing exchanges a stake in business ownership for capital, unlike debt financing which requires repayment with interest.

questions.question: Debt financing differs from equity financing primarily because debt financing:
options: Must be repaid with interest and does not dilute ownership
Gives the lender permanent ownership of the business
Never needs to be repaid under any circumstances
Automatically grants voting rights to the lender
questions.correct_answer: Must be repaid with interest and does not dilute ownership
questions.explanation: Debt financing (e.g. bank loans) obligates the borrower to repay principal plus interest, while the lender does not gain ownership in the business.

questions.question: An 'angel investor' is best described as:
options: A wealthy individual who provides capital to a start-up in exchange for equity or convertible debt
A government agency that issues business licenses
A bank offering only short-term overdraft facilities
An employee who works without any salary
questions.correct_answer: A wealthy individual who provides capital to a start-up in exchange for equity or convertible debt
questions.explanation: Angel investors are typically affluent individuals who fund early-stage start-ups, often in exchange for ownership equity or convertible debt.

questions.question: A microfinance bank, in the Nigerian financial system, primarily serves to:
options: Provide small loans and financial services to micro, small, and medium enterprises
Regulate the national currency exchange rate
Issue government treasury bonds exclusively
Serve only multinational corporations
questions.correct_answer: Provide small loans and financial services to micro, small, and medium enterprises
questions.explanation: Microfinance banks in Nigeria are licensed to provide financial services, especially credit, to low-income individuals and small businesses who often lack access to conventional bank loans.

questions.question: Crowdfunding, as a modern source of start-up finance, involves:
options: Raising small amounts of capital from a large number of people, typically via an online platform
Borrowing a single large loan from one commercial bank
Receiving funding exclusively from the federal government
Selling the entire company to one private buyer
questions.correct_answer: Raising small amounts of capital from a large number of people, typically via an online platform
questions.explanation: Crowdfunding pools small contributions from many individuals, often through digital platforms, to finance a business idea or project.

questions.question: A cooperative society, as a form of business enterprise, is primarily organized to:
options: Enable members to pool resources for mutual economic benefit
Maximize profit for a single external shareholder
Operate exclusively as a government parastatal
Avoid any form of member participation in decisions
questions.correct_answer: Enable members to pool resources for mutual economic benefit
questions.explanation: Cooperative societies are member-owned organizations formed to jointly meet common economic, social, and financial needs, such as access to credit.

questions.question: In a general partnership, the liability of the partners for business debts is typically:
options: Unlimited and joint, extending to their personal assets
Completely limited to the amount each partner initially invested
Borne entirely by only one designated partner
Nonexistent since partnerships have no liability
questions.correct_answer: Unlimited and joint, extending to their personal assets
questions.explanation: In a general partnership, partners are jointly and severally liable for business debts, meaning personal assets can be used to satisfy business obligations.

questions.question: A limited partnership differs from a general partnership in that a limited partnership includes:
options: At least one partner whose liability is restricted to their capital contribution
Only partners with unlimited liability
No possibility of any partner having limited liability
A requirement that all partners must be family members
questions.correct_answer: At least one partner whose liability is restricted to their capital contribution
questions.explanation: A limited partnership has general partners with unlimited liability and limited partners whose liability is capped at their investment.

questions.question: Franchising, as a growth and market-entry strategy, involves:
options: A franchisor granting a franchisee the right to operate a business using its brand and system for a fee
Two competing companies merging into a single new entity
A firm giving away its product for free indefinitely
A government agency taking over a private business
questions.correct_answer: A franchisor granting a franchisee the right to operate a business using its brand and system for a fee
questions.explanation: Franchising allows a franchisee to use an established brand's trademark, operating procedures, and support in return for franchise and royalty fees.

questions.question: A key advantage of buying a franchise, compared to starting an entirely new independent business, is:
options: Access to an established brand name and proven business model
Complete freedom to change the brand name at will
No ongoing fees are ever required
Total independence from any franchisor guidelines
questions.correct_answer: Access to an established brand name and proven business model
questions.explanation: Franchisees benefit from a tested business system, brand recognition, and ongoing franchisor support, which can reduce start-up risk compared to an independent venture.

questions.question: Market segmentation, applied by a growing small business, refers to:
options: Dividing a broad market into distinct groups of customers with similar needs
Selling a single product to every consumer without differentiation
Merging all competitors into one large market
Eliminating the need for any customer research
questions.correct_answer: Dividing a broad market into distinct groups of customers with similar needs
questions.explanation: Market segmentation groups customers by characteristics such as demographics or behavior so a business can target its marketing more effectively.

questions.question: The marketing mix ('4 Ps') used by small businesses to reach customers consists of:
options: Product, Price, Place, and Promotion
Profit, People, Policy, and Process only
Planning, Production, Personnel, and Payroll
Purchase, Payment, Postage, and Packaging
questions.correct_answer: Product, Price, Place, and Promotion
questions.explanation: The classic marketing mix framework identifies four controllable elements a business manages to satisfy its target market: Product, Price, Place, and Promotion.

questions.question: Pricing a product below competitors specifically to gain market share is known as:
options: Penetration pricing
Skimming pricing
Cost-plus pricing
Premium pricing
questions.correct_answer: Penetration pricing
questions.explanation: Penetration pricing sets an initially low price to quickly attract customers and build market share before potentially raising prices later.

questions.question: Price skimming, as a pricing strategy, involves:
options: Setting a high initial price for a new product and gradually lowering it over time
Setting the lowest possible price from the outset
Giving the product away entirely for free
Matching the exact price of every competitor
questions.correct_answer: Setting a high initial price for a new product and gradually lowering it over time
questions.explanation: Price skimming targets early adopters willing to pay a premium for a new product, with prices lowered progressively to reach broader market segments.

questions.question: Effective inventory management is important to a small business primarily because it helps:
options: Balance the cost of holding stock against the risk of running out of goods
Guarantee that a business will never incur any expenses
Eliminate the need for a business plan
Ensure the business never needs to purchase raw materials again
questions.correct_answer: Balance the cost of holding stock against the risk of running out of goods
questions.explanation: Good inventory management minimizes holding costs and stockouts, ensuring sufficient supply to meet demand without tying up excessive capital.

questions.question: A SWOT analysis conducted as part of a business plan helps an entrepreneur to:
options: Assess internal strengths and weaknesses alongside external opportunities and threats
Calculate the exact market price of raw materials
Replace the need for any market research
Determine the founder's personal tax obligations
questions.correct_answer: Assess internal strengths and weaknesses alongside external opportunities and threats
questions.explanation: SWOT analysis is a strategic planning tool that evaluates a venture's internal capabilities and the external environment to inform business decisions.

questions.question: A venture capitalist typically differs from an angel investor mainly because a venture capitalist:
options: Invests pooled institutional funds, often in larger amounts and at later stages of growth
Never requires any equity stake in return
Invests only their own personal money in very small amounts
Only funds government-owned enterprises
questions.correct_answer: Invests pooled institutional funds, often in larger amounts and at later stages of growth
questions.explanation: Venture capitalists manage pooled funds from institutions or wealthy investors and typically invest larger sums at growth stages, compared to individual angel investors at earlier stages.

questions.question: A trade credit arrangement allows a small business to:
options: Receive goods or services from a supplier now and pay for them at a later agreed date
Avoid ever paying its suppliers
Receive a government tax exemption automatically
Sell shares of the company to the supplier
questions.correct_answer: Receive goods or services from a supplier now and pay for them at a later agreed date
questions.explanation: Trade credit is a short-term financing arrangement where suppliers allow buyers to delay payment for goods received, easing the buyer's cash flow.

questions.question: A cash flow statement in a business plan primarily shows:
options: The inflows and outflows of cash over a specific period
The total number of employees in the firm
The physical location of all business assets
The founder's personal educational qualifications
questions.correct_answer: The inflows and outflows of cash over a specific period
questions.explanation: A cash flow statement tracks how cash moves in and out of a business, helping entrepreneurs manage liquidity and avoid running out of cash.

questions.question: Competitive analysis in a business plan is conducted to:
options: Identify competitors' strengths and weaknesses relative to the proposed business
Eliminate all existing competitors from the market immediately
Avoid the need to understand customer needs
Calculate the founder's monthly household budget
questions.correct_answer: Identify competitors' strengths and weaknesses relative to the proposed business
questions.explanation: Competitive analysis helps an entrepreneur understand the competitive landscape and position their business to gain an advantage over rivals.

questions.question: An entrepreneur choosing between a sole proprietorship and a limited liability company for a growing business would most likely favor the limited liability company primarily to:
options: Protect personal assets by limiting liability to the amount invested
Avoid ever paying any form of business tax
Eliminate the need for a business plan
Prevent the company from ever being sold
questions.correct_answer: Protect personal assets by limiting liability to the amount invested
questions.explanation: As a business grows and risk increases, limited liability protection becomes an important reason for entrepreneurs to incorporate rather than remain a sole proprietor.

questions.question: A start-up's 'value proposition' refers to:
options: The specific benefit and value a product or service delivers to customers
The total number of shares issued by the company
The company's registered office address
The founder's personal net worth
questions.correct_answer: The specific benefit and value a product or service delivers to customers
questions.explanation: The value proposition articulates why customers should choose a business's offering, based on the distinct benefit it provides relative to alternatives.

questions.question: Promotion, as one of the 4 Ps of the marketing mix, includes activities such as:
options: Advertising, sales promotion, and public relations
Setting the factory's production schedule
Determining the company's tax rate
Designing the organizational chart
questions.correct_answer: Advertising, sales promotion, and public relations
questions.explanation: Promotion covers all the communication tools a business uses to inform and persuade customers, including advertising, sales promotions, and PR.
